Proposition 5.7 Candidate rank computer
$D_5(Q)=1$ for every $2$-group $Q$ of order $2^{11}$, nilpotency class $3$ and rank $d(Q)\ge8$. More generally, every candidate $Q$ satisfies $|\Phi(Q)|\ge16$, that is, $d(Q)\le\log_2|Q|-4$.
The second statement is proved on paper (and in Lean); the first is derived from it and Proposition 5.3, so it is computer-assisted.
Proposition 5.10 Order 2¹¹ computer

$D_5(Q)=1$ for every $2$-group $Q$ of order $2^{11}$ and nilpotency class $3$. Consequently, a counterexample to Question 1.1 among finite $2$-groups of nilpotency class $3$ has order at least $2^{12}$. By computer.
Theorem 6.9 γ₂/γ₃ of exponent 3 paper

Let $Q$ be a finite $3$-group in which $\gamma_2(Q)/\gamma_3(Q)$ has exponent at most $3$, i.e. $[x^3,y]\in\gamma_3(Q)$ for all $x,y\in Q$. Then $D_5(Q)=\gamma_5(Q)$, whatever the invariants of $Q/\gamma_2(Q)$. More generally, $D_5(G)=\gamma_5(G)$ for any group $G$ in which $G/\gamma_2(G)$ is a finite $3$-group and $\gamma_2(G)/\gamma_3(G)$ has exponent at most $3$.
Theorem 6.10 γ₄³ = 1 and γ₂⁹ ⊆ γ₄ paper

Let $Q$ be a finite $3$-group of nilpotency class $\le4$ such that (H1) the exponent of $\gamma_4(Q)$ divides $3$ and (H2) $a^9\in\gamma_4(Q)$ for every $a\in\gamma_2(Q)$. Then $D_5(Q)=1$. More generally, $D_5(G)=\gamma_5(G)$ for every group $G$ such that $G/\gamma_2(G)$ is a finite $3$-group, $\gamma_4(G)^3\subseteq\gamma_5(G)$ and $\gamma_2(G)^9\subseteq\gamma_4(G)$.
Theorem 6.11 γ₄³ ⊆ γ₅ paper

Let $Q$ be a finite $3$-group of nilpotency class $\le4$ with $\gamma_4(Q)^3=1$. Then $D_5(Q)=1$. More generally, $D_5(G)=\gamma_5(G)$ for any group $G$ such that $G/\gamma_2(G)$ is a finite $3$-group and $\gamma_4(G)^3\subseteq\gamma_5(G)$.
Corollary 6.12 D₅ ⊆ γ₄³ paper

Let $Q$ be a finite $3$-group of nilpotency class $\le4$. Then $D_5(Q)\subseteq\gamma_4(Q)^3$. More generally, $D_5(G)\subseteq\gamma_4(G)^3\gamma_5(G)$ for any group $G$ such that $G/\gamma_2(G)$ is a finite $3$-group.
Theorem 6.19 3-groups of order up to 3⁹ computer

$D_5(Q)=\gamma_5(Q)$ for every $3$-group $Q$ of order at most $3^9$. Consequently, $D_5(G)/\gamma_5(G)$ has no $3$-torsion for every finite group $G$ whose Sylow $3$-subgroup has order at most $3^9$. By computer.
Open question §7, item 2 3-torsion in D₅/γ₅ open
Does $3$-torsion occur in $D_5(G)/\gamma_5(G)$ for some group $G$, i.e. is Tahara's bound $6$ for the exponent of $D_5/\gamma_5$ attained?

Known: there is no $3$-torsion if the Sylow $3$-subgroup has order $\le3^9$ (Theorem 6.19), and $D_5=\gamma_5$ if $G/\gamma_2$ is a finite $3$-group and $\gamma_4^3\subseteq\gamma_5$ (Theorem 6.11). A minimal $3$-group with $D_5\ne\gamma_5$ has order $\ge3^{10}$, class $4$, cyclic centre, $\gamma_2/\gamma_3$ of exponent $\ge9$ and cyclic $\gamma_4\le Z(Q)$ of order $\ge9$.
Open question §7, item 3 Group analogue of Theorem C open

The group analogue of Theorem C of Ionin–Mikhailov–Petrov: is $D_{2c-1}(G)=1$ for every metabelian group $G$ of nilpotency class $\le c$? For $c=3$ this is Question 1.1. The question reduces to finite metabelian $p$-groups; for odd $p$ the answer is positive for all $c$ (Gupta, 1991), so only the case $p=2$, $c\ge3$ is open.
